dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses MCP (screen/widget) framework typical of ORCA system.
evidence: COPY W01.INC through W09.INC screen area copybooks
no EXEC CICS / no EXEC SQL

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical institution (hospital ward) management settings within the JMA ORCA medical receipt billing system. Handles ward/department management (byoto kanri), nursing configuration, inpatient fee calculation parameters.
purpose.summary: ORCGW20 is a component of the JMA ORCA medical receipt software system responsible for hospital ward management information settings. It manages ward/room configuration, nursing ratios, inpatient fee calculation rules, and related master data for Japanese medical billing. The program uses an MCP-based screen framework with extensive COPY-based modular structure.

notable_features: 79 COPY statements indicating heavy modular copybook use
MCP widget-based screen framework (ORCA-specific, not CICS)
REDEFINES used extensively for code table overlays
S9(9) BINARY fields for state/row tracking
432 PERFORM statements indicating structured procedural logic
Hardcoded date constants for Japanese fiscal year reforms (H18=2006, H20=2008)
No COMP-3 usage despite financial domain
verdict.notes: File is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA (日医標準レセプトソフト) system. Comments are in Japanese EUC-JP encoding, decoded as latin-1 causing mojibake in the visible text. Source truncated at 16000 chars out of 234175 bytes / 6062 lines; full program not visible but structure is clear. Program type classified as online-cics equivalent because ORCA uses its own MCP screen framework analogous to CICS for interactive screen handling.
